title: Design System: Cody Butryn — The Estimate Packet

desk.note: Also punched through the paper as the perforation band's circles — the desk showing through the sheet is what makes the tear-off read as perforated.

paper-dim.note: Now also the ground of the terms panel, which is the largest single paper-dim region in the build.

canary.note: Carries a structural role beyond highlighting: it is the .sheet::before underlay — the customer's copy in the carbonless set, visible on every page as a 5px down-and-right margin.

pink.note: The .sheet::after underlay at 10px — the file copy, deepest in the set. Its only two uses (the triplicate section and the underlay) are the same stock.

rule.note: Drawn dotted in the terms panel's row dividers — the same hairline weight, a different stroke, which is how a printed form separates terms from table rows.

rule-strong.note: Also the staple's ink, the edge of both underlay copies, and the perforation's dashed top edge. The heavy rule is the system's 'edge of paper' color.

overlay.note: Defined only in gallery.html as --overlay; the one cool, non-paper surface in the system and the only backdrop that permits a neutral shadow. The alpha is load-bearing — the desk must stay faintly readable behind the plate.

print-page.note: Defined only in resume.html as --print-page and applied to body inside @media print. The system's only pure white; it exists because paper stock is the printer's job, not the stylesheet's. Never valid on screen.

display.purpose: The owner's name at the top-left of the letterhead. One per page, Franklin 900 uppercase in carbon blue, now carrying the carbon misregistration text-shadow. Index's .lh-name and the résumé's .lh-name are set identically; the gallery's h1 shares the ramp step at its own vw slope and a lighter 0.15-alpha misregistration.

headline.purpose: The largest step on the ramp, held by two things: the estimate's h1 (Courier Prime 700 in ink, capped at 24ch so it breaks like a typed entry) and the totals-strip figures, which now run the full clamp(1.5rem,3.1vw,2.35rem) at -0.03em. Those figures are the page's display type — on a real estimate the biggest number is the total.

title.purpose: Section headings. Inseparable from their 3px double top rule and 1px bottom rule.

subtitle.purpose: Work-order names, copy-set headings, gallery card titles, résumé job titles.

body.purpose: Pre-printed explanatory copy in carbon-soft, max 62ch.

typed.purpose: Every value entered for this customer: contact lines, scope values, results, résumé bullets and profile, gallery notes and card titles, the terms rows, the stub's remittance line, fine print.

label.purpose: Field names, column heads, box headers, tab text, signature captions, the copy-set edge marks, the terms panel's reversed carbon header, the stub's caps kicker-free instruction line. The workhorse of the printed voice.

stamp.purpose: Stamps, badges, and buttons share this voice, which is what makes the CTA feel like part of the form. The availability stamp scales between the label and typed steps and now sits in its own right-aligned .stamp-row band rather than an absolute corner.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: The main sheet and the clipped screenshots. The strongest elevation in the system.

shadows.name: card-rest
shadows.purpose: Work orders, copy sheets, gallery cards at rest.

shadows.name: card-lift
shadows.purpose: Filed-card hover, paired with translateY(-3px). Fine-pointer only.

shadows.name: nav-hairline
shadows.purpose: Separates the sticky folder-tab bar from the desk. A rule drawn as a shadow.

shadows.name: lightbox-plate
shadows.purpose: The enlarged gallery image over the overlay scrim — the only non-warm shadow, because the backdrop is not paper.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The system's only easing curve, tokenized as --ease-out in all three files. Every transition and the stamp impression use it.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Active press on controls: scale(0.97) on buttons and tabs, scale(0.99) on cards and totals cells. Fires on touch as well as pointer.

motion.name: tint
motion.purpose: Hover fill changes on buttons, tabs, and totals cells.

motion.name: stamp-press
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: scale(1.25) → scale(1) at the stamp's rotation, fired once by IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.6 then unobserved.

motion.name: stamp-press-reduced
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion branch: the scale is dropped and only the fade remains.

physicalDevices.name: The Set
physicalDevices.purpose: Two pseudo-element underlays offset down-and-right so every page reads as a carbonless set: white on top, canary customer copy beneath, pink file copy deepest. Applied on all three surfaces. Below 640px they collapse to a downward-only peek (inset:0 0 -4px 0 / 0 0 -8px 0) so the set never pushes past the viewport edge; hidden outright in @media print, because a printed page is one sheet.

physicalDevices.name: Staple
physicalDevices.purpose: A 26px authored inline SVG through the top-left corner of the set, with two faint legs at 0.55 opacity implying the back of the stack. Drops to 19px at 9px inset below 640px. Decorative, non-interactive, hidden in print.

physicalDevices.name: Carbon misregistration
physicalDevices.purpose: The second impression landing a hair off the first, on the index and résumé letterhead names; the gallery h1 runs the same offset at 0.15 alpha. Deliberately carbon and never stamp red, because red is state. This is a printing artifact drawn in type, not an elevation shadow — it is recorded here rather than in the shadow vocabulary so nothing inherits a hard offset box-shadow from it.

physicalDevices.name: Perforation
physicalDevices.value: .perf{height:15px;margin:0 calc(clamp(1.1rem,4vw,3rem) * -1);background-image:radial-gradient(circle 3.2px at 11px 7.5px, var(--desk) 97%, transparent 100%);background-size:22px 15px;background-repeat:repeat-x;border-top:1px dashed var(--rule-strong)}
physicalDevices.purpose: A 15px band of desk-colored circles punched through the paper on a 22px repeat over a dashed heavy-rule edge, spanning the full sheet width by negating the gutter. The one place the desk shows through the sheet.

physicalDevices.name: Sheet and stamp rotation
physicalDevices.purpose: Rotation stays at or under 1.5° for anything made of paper; only stamps rotate visibly. The initials box is the sole hand-annotation rotation.

notes: There is no shared stylesheet: the :root token block is duplicated verbatim in the <style> head of index.html, gallery.html, and resume.html. Any token change is a three-file edit. Surface-only tokens are the deliberate exception — --overlay is declared in gallery.html only and --print-page in resume.html only, because each has exactly one host surface.

The Set, the staple, and the misregistration are also duplicated across all three heads for the same reason. A new surface that omits them has left the world; a page rendered as a lone white sheet is off-system.

Radius is tokenized in all three files as --r-tab (6px), --r-stamp (5px), --r-badge (3px), --r-scroll (7px). Each file declares only the radii it uses: index has all four, gallery has tab/badge/scroll, resume has tab/scroll. The underlay copies, the staple, the terms panel, the initials box, and the stub are all square — none of them introduced a new radius.

The folder-tab shape is a rule, not a token: rounded.tab is a single scalar corner radius and the top-two-corners shape lives in the CSS as border-radius: var(--r-tab) var(--r-tab) 0 0. A radius linter that stringifies the four resolved corners will report the tab as unmatched; both constituent values (rounded.tab and rounded.none) are documented, and no shorthand token should be invented to silence it.

The totals figures moved from the title step to the headline step — clamp(1.5rem,3.1vw,2.35rem), letter-spacing -0.03em, line-height 1.05 — making them the page's display type. The system deliberately has no oversized statement headline: anything that needs to shout here shouts as a number.

The index hero is a 1.55fr / 1fr grid (.job-top) collapsing to one column at 860px; the availability stamp left absolute positioning for a right-aligned .stamp-row band under the letterhead rule, left-aligned below 860px, because it collided with the terms panel header.

The terms panel adds one more reversed carbon caps bar and one more all-caps run to the detector's tallies. Both are the printed voice of a form doing exactly what a form does; they are this world's grammar, not new defects.

The résumé's print output is a shipping surface. Its two-column grid collapses to one column in print through the 820px breakpoint (US Letter measures under 820 CSS px), not through a print-specific override. The print block also hides the staple and both underlay copies.
Stamps are visible by default; the 'js' class set inline on <html> opts into the animation, so a JS failure leaves them printed rather than invisible.
Every font size in the build resolves to a step of the documented type ramp; the terms rows and stub line landed on the existing typed and label steps rather than introducing new sizes.

narrative.overview:
This is a website that behaves like paperwork a trade owner already signs weekly. A single warm sheet of paper sits on a slightly darker counter; on that sheet, everything the visitor needs is set as a form: a letterhead with numbered boxes, a scope-of-work table with line items and reference numbers, work orders with results and a PAID stamp, a triplicate copy set, and an acceptance block with a signature line. The persuasion is structural, not rhetorical — proof reads as line items and stamped totals rather than as hero copy and case-study scroll.

The system runs on a strict two-voice split that is the whole personality: the form is printed, the answers are typed. Anything pre-printed on the blank (labels, section bars, the letterhead name, buttons, box headers) is Libre Franklin in heavy weights, uppercase, wide-tracked, in carbon blue. Anything filled in for this particular customer (headline, results, contact, prose in the copies, résumé bullets) is Courier Prime in near-black ink. A reader can tell blank-form from fill-in at a glance without reading a word, and that legibility is the system's core asset.

Density is high and deliberately un-airy: hairline rules, double-rule section bars, small caps labels at 0.72rem, tables that stay tables. Depth is paper-thin — the sheet and the cards float on soft, warm, double-layer ambient shadows, never hard-offset ones. One color, the red stamp ink, carries every piece of state in the system (availability, PAID, job numbers, dates, sample badges) and is used nowhere else. The build refuses the designer-portfolio hero: no full-bleed image lede, no oversized centered statement type, no case-study scroll.
keyCharacteristics: Two faces, one job each: printed Franklin caps vs. typed Courier fill-ins
Square corners everywhere except the folder tabs that name the metaphor
One red ink for every state, used sparingly enough to stay loud
Rules and boxes, not cards-with-radius; borders do the structural work
Ambient warm shadows only; the sheet lifts, nothing else pops
One authored motion moment (stamps pressing on), then stillness

rules.name: The One Stamp Ink Rule
rules.body: Red is state, and state only: availability, PAID, and reference numbers. If a new element needs red for emphasis rather than for status, it does not get red — it gets a canary highlight or carbon weight.

rules.name: The Printed-vs-Typed Rule
rules.body: Carbon blue means the form printed it; ink black-brown means someone typed it in. Never set a filled-in value in carbon blue, and never set a pre-printed label in ink.

rules.name: The Warm Ground Rule
rules.body: No pure white and no pure black anywhere on screen. Paper is the paper token, the ground is the desk token, text is the ink token. Pure #fff appears only in the résumé's print stylesheet, where the physical page supplies the paper.

rules.name: The Two-Face Rule
rules.body: There are two fonts and no third. New type needs are solved by moving between Franklin's weights (400/600/700/800/900) and Courier's two, not by adding a face.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every figure that reads as a total, a reference, a phone number, or a date carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (the .num class). Numbers are the product here; they must line up.

rules.name: The Caps-Get-Tracking Rule
rules.body: Uppercase text is never set at default tracking. Labels take 0.14–0.16em, tabs and stamps 0.10–0.12em, section bars 0.09em, the display name 0.015em. Tracking falls as size rises.

rules.name: The Print Is A Layout Rule
rules.body: On the résumé, print is a first-class breakpoint: navigation, the acceptance strip, the print button, and the fine print are hidden; the sheet drops its border, shadow, margin, max-width, and padding so the paper becomes the sheet; links lose underlines; jobs and skill groups get break-inside: avoid. The two-column grid collapses to one column in print via the existing 820px breakpoint (a US Letter page measures under 820 CSS px), not via a print-specific override — so any change to that breakpoint changes the printed résumé. print-color-adjust: exact is set on body so carbon rules and stamp-red dates survive to paper.

rules.name: The Paper-Only Elevation Rule
rules.body: Only things that are sheets of paper cast shadows. Boxes, stamps, tags, chips, table rows, and buttons are printed on the paper and are flat forever.

rules.name: The Hover-Is-A-Fine-Pointer Rule
rules.body: Every lift, background shift, and color hover is wrapped in @media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine). Touch devices get the :active press (scale(0.97) on controls, scale(0.99) on cards) instead — no sticky hover states on phones, which is the primary device here.

rules.name: The Set Is Not Decoration Rule
rules.body: The canary and pink underlays are the same two stocks named in the triplicate process section. If a new surface is added, it inherits the set; a page rendered as a lone white sheet has left the world.

dos: Do set every new element in the printed-vs-typed split: Franklin caps for what the form printed, Courier for what was filled in.
Do reserve the stamp red for state and reference numbers, and keep it under a handful of appearances per screen.
Do build structure from borders — 1px hairlines, 1.5px field rectangles, 3px double rules at divisions — rather than from radius or fill.
Do put .num (tabular figures) on every total, phone number, date, and job reference.
Do gate every hover behind @media (hover:hover) and (pointer:fine) and give touch a scale(0.97)/scale(0.99) press instead.
Do keep motion to the one stamp impression: enter once, unobserve, and honor prefers-reduced-motion by dropping the scale.
Do make new content degrade without JavaScript — the js class opt-in pattern means the default state must already be correct.
Do treat the résumé's print output as a shipping surface: check any layout change at page width, since print inherits the 820px breakpoint.
Do letterbox artwork inside the fixed 4:3 image well (object-fit: contain on a paper-dim ground) when its own lettering must survive, rather than varying card heights.
donts: Don't add a third typeface, or use a system display face. Franklin's five weights and Courier's two cover every need in this system.
Don't use pure white or pure black on screen; the only #fff in the system is the print stylesheet's page.
Don't apply hard offset shadows, glows, or colored shadows. Shadows are two-layer warm ambient stacks, and only paper sheets get them.
Don't round corners on anything other than folder tabs, stamps, badges, and the scrollbar. Cards, boxes, and buttons stay square.

Don't introduce decorative eyebrows or kickers above headings. Small caps text above a heading is permitted only when it is a real form field with a real value (PREPARED FOR: …, SCOPE, RESULT) — a label with nothing filled in is not a field, it is decoration.
Don't use glyph or icon-font icons. The four icons in the build (external link, paperclip, signature, favicon wordmark) are inline SVG stroked in currentColor; new icons follow that.

Don't hard-code hex values that a token already covers, and don't add new untokenized ink tints. Several body greys (#3E3A32, #33302A, #5C564B, #5C6B80) and the carbon hover (#16304F) drifted in as literals; new work uses the ink, carbon-soft, or carbon-deep tokens.

Don't let the token block drift between pages. There is no shared stylesheet (static site, no build step), so :root is duplicated verbatim in all three <style> heads — any token change must be applied to index.html, gallery.html, and resume.html in the same edit.
Don't style with inline style attributes. A handful survive in the build; they are debt, not a pattern.
Don't rotate sheets more than 1°. Only stamps rotate visibly (−6° / −8°).
Don't reintroduce the designer-portfolio hero: no full-bleed image lede, no centered oversized statement type, no case-study scroll. Proof arrives as line items, totals, and stamps.
